headline: Visayas Grid Faces Red and Yellow Alerts Again as Available Capacity Trails Demand
seoTitle: Visayas Grid Under Red, Yellow Alerts Again on August 26 | FMB News
seoDescription: NGCP placed the Visayas grid under red and yellow alerts again on August 26 as available capacity stood at 2,324 MW against projected peak demand of 2,550 MW.
deck: NGCP projected 2,324 MW of available capacity against 2,550 MW of peak demand, with multiple generating units unavailable or derated.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Visayas grid was placed under red and yellow alerts again on Wednesday as generation capacity remained constrained by forced outages and derated power plants, according to the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines.
The red alert was scheduled from 3:00 PM to 9:00 PM, with yellow alerts from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM and again from 9:00 PM to 10:00 PM.

sections.heading: Capacity and outages
paragraphs: NGCP projected available capacity at 2,324 megawatts against peak demand of 2,550 MW.

Units 1 and 2 of Therma Visayas Inc. and Unit 1 of Kepco SPC Power Corp. remained unavailable. NGCP also reported additional forced outages and 14 plants operating at derated capacity, bringing total unavailable or reduced capacity to about 901 MW.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: NGCP issues a yellow alert when operating reserves fall below contingency requirements. A red alert applies when supply is insufficient to meet consumer demand and the grid's regulating requirement.
The Visayas grid was also under red and yellow alerts on August 25, when available capacity was projected at 2,421 MW against peak demand of 2,570 MW.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated grid alerts indicate a narrow operating margin and increase the risk that utilities may need demand-management measures when additional generation becomes unavailable or demand exceeds forecasts.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Consumers and businesses in the Visayas should monitor NGCP and distribution-utility advisories for changes to alert periods, restoration of unavailable generating units and any demand-management measures.
